1. Playbook Claude Critic spawn: pointer required; launcher-dependent Windows limits (cmd/batch 8191 vs CreateProcessW 32767 including null); no false CreateProcess ~8191 sole string.
2. Pong proves probe only.
3. Thin skill/contract pointers; no AGENTS fat prose; no new halt token; no evaluateN3LaunchProbe change.

items.title: Playbook: pointer required + launcher-dependent Windows limits

narrative.Acceptance: In Critic spawn (second recipe) under Claude: require envelope under arc dest + short pointer prompt for Claude critic spawn on all hosts. Name launcher-dependent Windows command-line limits: cmd.exe/batch paths have an 8,191-character limit; CreateProcessW permits 32,767 characters including the terminating null. These are whole-command limits, not a prompt-only allowance. Do not bind the false sole string CreateProcess ~8191.
State that launch-probe pong-ok proves only that probe invocation under critic argv; it proves neither long-prompt transport nor envelope read/completion.
Thin skill/contract pointers only — no fat Windows prose in AGENTS.md; no new halt token; no evaluateN3LaunchProbe / seat-composition change.
Cross-link #5478 as the adjacent post-pointer hang class (0-byte with CPU after pointer). Do not collapse with argv/command-line length empty-exit class; leave #5478 diagnosis/fix on that issue.

Extend design_critique_contract tests to pin required playbook/contract pointer strings for Windows launcher-dependent limits and pong-only-proves-probe language where those surfaces are locked by the contract suite.

sentences: docs(design-critique,windows): name CreateProcess argv ceiling for Claude critic pointer spawn

Summary `content/docs/grok-build-subscription-setup.md` § Design-critique dispatch already requires the Claude critic pointer form (`claude -p "Read and follow <envelope-path>"`) and forbids putting the full envelope on stdin / as raw probe text.
It does not name the Windows CreateProcess ~8191-character argv limit as the reason full `-p` envelopes fail closed (immediate empty exit / empty logs) even when a tiny launch-probe pong returns rc0.
Parents on Windows Grok Build currently recover that knowledge from host-memory / session notes rather than a Directive playbook limb.
That gap makes the pointer recipe look optional or “style,” and re-teaches the same failure: launch-probe green → full envelope as `-p` → empty critic.
Desired outcome 1.
Document in `content/docs/grok-build-subscription-setup.md` Critic spawn (second recipe), under Claude: - On Windows, do not pass the full critic envelope via `claude -p` (CreateProcess argv ~8191).
Write the envelope under the arc dest (e.g.
`.deft-scratch/critic-claude.md`), then pass only a short pointer prompt.
Tiny launch-probe pong green does not prove a full-envelope `-p` will launch.
Keep Normative stop ownership on the existing Envelope and ceiling / #4432 launch-probe; this is playbook hardening, not a new halt token.
Cross-link open hang residue `#5478` (pointer already used, still 0-byte hang) so parents do not collapse “argv too long” and “hung after pointer” into one diagnosis.
Out of scope - Fixing the post-pointer 0-byte hang itself (`#5478`).
Changing `evaluateN3LaunchProbe` / seat-composition fixtures.
Making paste-ready the default Claude seat.
Acceptance - [ ] Playbook names Windows argv ceiling + pointer-required for Claude critic spawn.
[ ] Playbook states launch-probe pong ≠ full-envelope launch proof.
[ ] Skill / contract stay thin pointers (no fat Windows prose in AGENTS.md).
[ ] `#5478` cited as related hang class, not the same defect.
